title: 8.4 A 4GHz, 0.69%-Accuracy Voltage-Droop Detector with Multiple Remote Sensing and Under 2-Cycle Detection Latency in 2nm GAAFET
problem: Voltage droop detection in modern SoCs requires both PVT-tolerant direct sensing and remote-capable distributed detection; previous digital detectors (TDC-based) suffer from PVT sensitivity and low conversion gain; analog detectors have bulky blocks, limited integration, and routing/frequency constraints.
motivation: Per-core voltage scaling to minimize power consumption is critical in modern SoCs but requires accurate, fast droop detection to prevent supply violations.
method: The detector spreads tiny voltage-sensing circuits (called remote droop detectors, or RDD) across the chip that continuously sample at up to 4GHz. A central control circuit (droop detection controller, or DDC) coordinates all these distributed sensors and automatically adjusts for manufacturing variations and environmental conditions (PVT tolerance), keeping them synchronized. Together, they detect voltage droop in under 2 clock cycles with 0.69% accuracy, implemented in 2nm transistor technology.
key_novelty: Instead of a single bulky centralized detector, this design distributes tiny voltage sensors across the chip with centralized coordination that adapts to manufacturing and temperature variations, enabling high-speed detection everywhere without routing problems.
contributions: PVT-tolerant centralized control without analog blocks
primary_theme: Fast distributed voltage droop detection for per-core power scaling
